claims.text: The initial high-entropy-alloy intermediate layers have suboptimal heat-transfer performance.
Discontinuous interfacial microstructure causes the suboptimal heat-transfer performance of the initial layers.
Laser cladding an Inconel 718 transition layer onto the high-entropy-alloy substrate will produce a graded interface.
The laser-cladded Inconel 718 interface will improve microstructural continuity between layers.
The graded interface will reduce thermal boundary resistance.
Reduced thermal boundary resistance will improve heat transfer.
Inconel 718 has sufficient high-temperature strength and thermal stability to help preserve structural integrity under cyclic loading.
The laser-cladded samples will have lower thermal resistance than conventional high-entropy-alloy intermediate layers lacking the Inconel 718 transition layer.
The laser-cladded samples will avoid significant degradation of mechanical integrity over time.
The predicted thermal and structural benefits will hold at approximately 700–900 degrees Celsius under cyclic thermal and mechanical loading.
Temperatures of approximately 700–900 degrees Celsius and cyclic thermal and mechanical loads are typical operating conditions for plasma-facing reactor components.
Performance outside the specified temperature and loading conditions may not exhibit the predicted benefits.
The magnitude of thermal-conductivity improvement and long-term durability depend on laser-cladding parameters and in-service plasma effects.
